ADVISORY (not yet blocking this task) — F22 (P1, OPEN, NEW, tenth PR #325 Copilot review, HEAD 914cb214).

Plan §3.2 terminates three post-`LOCKING` failure edges (BOOTSTRAPPING fatal, RESOLVING no-copilot-exe, LAUNCHING spawn-error) directly at FAILED without passing through DRAINING — and DRAINING is where the plan places LOCK RELEASE. Combined with this task's own fail-closed stale-lock policy (§3.4: stale lock requires an explicit operator `--force-unlock`, never auto-broken), a routine pre-RUNNING failure leaves the workspace permanently locked until the operator finds and runs --force-unlock.

WHY THIS TASK IS IMPLICATED EVEN THOUGH THE DEFECT IS IN THE STATE MACHINE: the operator has two ways to close the hole. (1) Fix the transition table in 119.003-T so every post-LOCKING terminal exit routes through DRAINING — this task is then unchanged, and the fix is confined to 128-S. (2) Put the guarantee HERE, making release structural rather than caller-dependent — e.g. acquisition returns a scope guard / context manager whose exit always releases, so no reachable termination path can leak the lock regardless of what the state machine does. Option (2) is the more robust design (it cannot be re-broken by a later transition-table edit) but it ADDS A DoD OBLIGATION AND TESTS TO THIS TASK, which is a member of 127-S — the otherwise-eligible first shipment.

This comment is recorded so that whoever implements T5 does not lock in an API that makes option (2) impossible. It does NOT by itself block 127-S; 127-S is already blocked by F17. Stage adopted no resolution and changed no dependency edge.

Detail: docs/reviews/2026-08-09-copilot-cli-supervisor-control-plane-review.md (Cycle 4, tenth Copilot pass).

BLOCKING — F27 (P1, OPEN, NEW, raised by the fifteenth PR #325 Copilot review of HEAD 1f14795e, AFTER the 3-cycle plan-review budget was exhausted). THIS FINDING LANDS ON A 127-S MEMBER, i.e. on the eligible cursor.

DEFECT: this task defines the single-active-session invariant — the core safety property of the whole program (H2/H4) — but never requires ATOMIC ACQUISITION. It specifies a lockfile recording PID + process start-time, a liveness check using PID plus start-time, fail-closed REFUSED on contention, stale detection, force-unlock, path containment, and tests for "acquire/release, contention -> REFUSED, stale detection, force-unlock, recycled-PID rejection, crash-without-release cleanup, and path containment."

Every one of those is a check-then-act sequence. NOTHING requires the acquire step itself to be atomic, and NO test exercises SIMULTANEOUS contenders. The result is a textbook TOCTOU race: two supervisors starting at the same moment can both observe "no live lock", both write the lockfile, and both proceed — producing exactly the concurrent sessions this module exists to prevent. The listed contention test is inherently SEQUENTIAL (a holder already exists, a second attempt is refused), so it cannot detect this. The invariant can therefore be violated while every acceptance criterion passes.

WHY THIS IS P1 AND NOT COSMETIC: single-active is not a convenience property here. Two live supervisors on one workspace means two writers to the same session journal, two holders of the same workspace lock path, and — combined with F22 — two independent lock-release paths. The whole fail-closed design rests on it.

RESOLUTION (operator decision; Stage adopted none): require an ATOMIC create primitive for acquisition — O_CREAT|O_EXCL (os.open with exclusive creation) or an OS-level advisory lock — such that acquisition either succeeds exclusively or fails, with no observable window between test and write. Add a SIMULTANEOUS-CONTENDER test (N processes/threads racing to acquire, asserting exactly one success and N-1 REFUSED). Note the stale-lock path needs the same care: reclaiming a stale lock must not reintroduce the window.

NOTE ON THE ELIGIBLE CURSOR: 118.005-T is a member of 127-S, so this is the SECOND open P1 landing on the first shipment (F17 is the other), and F22's lock-release obligation may add a third. Detail: docs/reviews/2026-08-09-copilot-cli-supervisor-control-plane-review.md.
